races.title: State Assembly, District 57
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Sade Elhawary
cands.bio: Democrat and member of the California State Assembly for District 57 since December 2024. A former high school history teacher, college counselor and youth organizer at Community Coalition in South Los Angeles. She was Youth Engagement Campaign Manager on Karen Bass's 2022 mayoral campaign. She is a foster parent.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Working Families Party and YIMBY Action.
Her campaign site lists endorsements from Mayor Karen Bass, LA County Supervisors Holly J. Mitchell and Hilda Solis, Assemblymember Isaac Bryan, and the Los Angeles Times.

cands.gaps: We found no list of bills she has sponsored or authored; the Ballotpedia table was empty in the page we read. We found no documented statements or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B, gun policy, or a pledge on refusing specific kinds of contributions. Her site says she 'will not be bought by powerful special interests,' but gives no detail. Her campaign site's priorities page was cut off before the end, so its public-safety and equality lists were not fully read. Her stated positions come from her campaign site and a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, so they are promises rather than actions in office. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2024. Earlier she was a credentialed high school history teacher, a college counselor, and a youth organizer at Community Coalition since 2011, and she managed youth engagement on Karen Bass's 2022 mayoral campaign.
qual.why: She has held a legislative seat since December 2024, which counts toward the high range. Her pre-office work was in education and community organizing, with no law or budget career shown, so the score sits below the top of the range.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports California providing the full range of reproductive services, including abortion care, and says she will not back down in protecting access.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said she would ease the permitting and land-use entitlement process and cut red tape to speed housing construction. Her campaign site also says she wants to give Black and Brown communities a voice in neighborhood development decisions to block gentrification.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she wants to end over-policing as the public safety response and supports community-led alternatives to policing, funded through prevention-based social programs.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says she would work to increase teacher pay to attract teachers and reduce turnover. It also says she would greatly increase per-pupil spending in public schools. It does not address vouchers, charters or school choice.

roots.summary: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Los Angeles, and her own 2024 survey response and campaign site say she was born and raised in Los Angeles and attended local public K-12 schools.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she said California's cost to build is too high and that she would cut red tape, streamline development and ease permitting and land-use entitlement so housing development doesn't stagnate. She also said she favors using underutilized and vacant commercial spaces.

cands.name: Constance Jewel Menzies
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 57 in 2026. Ballotpedia lists her profession as educator; she describes herself as a postal worker, nurse, caregiver and school site president. She holds an associate degree from Los Angeles Trade-Technical College and two University of Phoenix degrees. No elected office is listed.

endorsements.text: She lists the California Republican Assembly, KEEP orange RED and Reform California as endorsers in her Ballotpedia survey. Ballotpedia also lists Reform California and several voter-guide recommendations (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Constance Menzies was born or raised, where she lives, or when she came to California. We found no record of any elected or appointed office. Her work history (postal worker, nurse, educator, school site president) comes only from her own survey answers and a brief Ballotpedia profile, with no employers or dates. We found no documented actions or votes on data centers, property taxes, housing and land, growth limits, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no stated positions on those topics beyond general support for law enforcement, strong schools and workforce training. We found no news coverage or controversies. Her campaign website is mostly template text with placeholder sections and gives no detailed platform.
